meta.what_it_proves: No string literal shaped like a chip part number (a short letter prefix, two to five digits, a short alphanumeric suffix) reaches tools/build_db.py's own source as a hardcode, except the entries named below, each with a reason no alternative exists.
meta.what_it_does_not_prove: That a surviving constant's VALUE is electrically or decode-correct, that no part-specific hardcode exists in a shape this pattern does not admit, or that the shipped tools/datasheet_overrides.json entries (a sibling JSON file, not scanned here) are themselves correct.
meta.how_it_was_derived: find_part_specific_constants() in tests/test_build_db_constant_census.py, ast.parse over the live tools/build_db.py source text, walking every ast.Constant string value, filtered by the shape_pattern above, with an empty allow-list so every shape match surfaces.
meta.how_to_update: Re-run find_part_specific_constants() against the live tools/build_db.py with an empty allow-list. Add every new survivor here with a non-empty reason recorded before committing -- never delete a survivor from this file to make an inconvenient finding disappear, and never widen or narrow shape_pattern in tests/test_build_db_constant_census.py to make a survivor appear or vanish without recording why in the same commit.

constants.line_context: if pinout_key is not None and pinout_key.startswith("DIP28"):
constants.reason: This is a pinout-FAMILY prefix test inside classify()'s SRAM/FRAM re-route arm, not a chip part number -- it groups every pinout key beginning with the DIP28_* family (DIP28_2764, DIP28_28C64, DIP28_28C256, DIP28_JEDEC_SRAM_8K, ...) so the arm can re-route any 28-pin SRAM-class chip regardless of which specific DIP28 pinout it resolved to. It matches the shape pattern only by coincidence: 'DIP' (3 letters) + '28' (2 digits) + zero further characters. No alternative representation of 'any DIP28-family pinout' avoids the shape match without either abandoning the string-prefix test (pinout keys are plain strings defined in pinouts.json, not an enum) or building a second family-membership table whose only content would be the same fact this prefix test already states directly. It selects a PINOUT FAMILY, never one PART; deleting or overriding it corresponds to no single chip.
